extracted.intended_audience: bibliometric researchers, science librarians, journal editors, and research managers
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and criteria for identifying core journals, mapping research-fronts, and interpreting citation/co-citation data (using SCI/SCf data) to describe relationships between fields (here: physical chemistry and chemical physics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core journal selection (SCF/SCI indexed core journals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of a set of 'core' periodicals indexed by the SCF/SCI (here: 31 physical chemistry/chemical physics journals indexed in 1983).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 lists the 31 core physical chemistry/chemical physics journals indexed by the SCF in 1983; these are the basis for counting 1983 articles and identifying which journals most prominently represent the fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-front definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A research front consists of a group of current papers that cite one or more older well-cited papers (the 'core' papers); the front is identified from SCI research-front data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use groups of current citing papers and their common references to identify fronts; the front includes the core papers and the citing papers, and can be used to identify which journals and topics are central to that front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for research-front journal inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of 'research-front journals' that cite the research front at or above a threshold number of citing documents (table labels indicate A = research-front journals that cite the research at least [threshold] citing documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper labels columns (A,B,C,D) to capture: A = research-front journals meeting a citing-document threshold; B = title; C = number of 1983 articles from core journals; D = number of core journal articles that cite the research-front. Use explicit numeric thresholds when available to define inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting 1983 articles from core journals (representation metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each research front, count the number of 1983 articles published in the predefined core journals (column C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the number of front papers published in core journals to the total number of front papers to gauge how concentrated a front is in the core set (examples: fronts with ~260 papers of which X were in core journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting core documents cited by a front (core-document citation metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count how many core documents (older well-cited papers) are cited by the front (e.g., a front citing 95 core documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the number of core documents cited to characterize the front's intellectual lineage and the extent to which it depends on a comparatively small set of highly cited works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-front size as significance indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the absolute number of papers in a research front (e.g., '1,100 papers were published in front #83-0023') as a measure of that front's prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both total papers in the front and how many of those appear in the core journals to indicate prominence and distribution across journal types (core vs. non-core).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-citation map interpretation (node/line semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation rules for co-citation maps: nodes represent co-citation strength; lines indicate semantic/relationship distance; numeric labels are for identification only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure captions: 'nodes represent co-citation strength, and distance is an indicator of semantic distance. Serial numbers are for identification only. Lines between nodes indicate relationships.' Use node size, label, and inter-node distance to read clusters and topic proximity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic labeling of fronts (thematic clustering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign thematic labels to mapped fronts (e.g., 'Molecular-orbital studies on catalysis and adsorption') based on the cluster's prevailing topics and representative keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative front descriptors and key topic phrases (as shown in Table 2 / Figure 2) to name and summarize each front; include sub-fronts and their applied/basic splits where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal citation-history analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the chronological distribution of citations to particular seminal papers (e.g., graphing citations from 1955–1984 for Gibbs's paper) to understand delayed recognition or long-term influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot citation counts over time to reveal patterns such as rediscovery, lagged recognition, or recent surges; use such curves to contextualize a paper's role in multiple fronts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SCI research-front data to identify current concerns/topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine SCI/SCF research-front tables and maps to identify current concerns and topical research fronts (e.g., catalysis, spectroscopy, photoelectrochemical cells, electronic-structure calculations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract fronts and their topic lists from SCI data (see Table 2 examples) and interpret which subfields and techniques are most active at a given time (1983 in this study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic (country-by-country) analysis of citing affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the percentage/count of citing papers by country for a given research front (Table 3 shows percent of front items citing #83-3402 by country).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use country-affiliation distributions to provide a national-level perspective on contributions to a front, highlighting dominant producer countries and international participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying seminal works and influential authors via citation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use citation counts (SCI citation tallies) to single out seminal works and highly cited authors (examples in text: Gibbs, Hammett, Slater; counts such as 624 citations or 'over 3,200 times since 1955').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report citation tallies from SCI and co-citation information to justify labeling a work as 'classic' or 'core' and to discuss awards/recognition and continued influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing core vs. non-core journal publication patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how much of a front's literature appears in 'core' journals versus non-core journals to understand dissemination patterns across the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show many front papers published outside the 31 core journals; use this comparison when judging whether a front is concentrated or widely dispersed across publication venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of detailed maps and submaps to reveal cross-field links
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce maps (and submaps) to reveal connections between disciplines (e.g., chemistry, physics, biochemistry) and to locate fronts that sit at disciplinary interfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's figures illustrate that mapping can show borderland regions and points (e.g., point #38 linking chemistry to biochemistry); use these visualizations to argue for interdependence or separation of subfields.
